articles.summary: The 2026 MTV VMAs are in full swing, and music’s biggest stars are showing up and out on the red carpet. Hosted by Snoop Dogg, this year’s Video Music Awards promises audiences a jam-packed program, including a performance from Madonna (her first at the show in more than two decades), a Dolly…
body: In addition to Madonna and Musgraves, the night’s lineup is set to include performances from LISA, RAYE, Shaboozey, Gunna, Sienna Spiro, GENER8ION and Yung Lean. For RAYE and Sienna Spiro, the performance will be their VMAs debut. Shaboozey will perform “Cowgirl” and then join Gunna for the first broadcast performance of their collaboration “High Noon,” while LISA will debut her new single “SaWaDiKa” on television. GENER8ION and Yung Lean will premiere “STORM II” onstage.

Kacey Musgraves will perform the tribute to Parton, making her first appearance on the VMAs stage in five years. She is nominated for best country for “Dry Spell” this year. RAYE, Sombr and Teddy Swims will perform a tribute to George Michael. 34 years since Nirvana first performed at the VMAs in 1992, the band is set to receive this year’s Video Vanguard Award.
In addition to her video premiere, Swift will also be honored with the inaugural Artist-Director Award.
The 2026 MTV VMAs air live Sunday, Sept. 27 at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Learn how to stream the show here.

articles.title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Co-Director Explains It’s ‘Very Difficult’ to Evolve Marvel Characters, but ‘We Need to Surprise Ourselves’ and ‘Audiences’
articles.summary: “Avengers: Doomsday” co-director Anthony Russo has opened up about the pressure that comes with evolving the franchise’s iconic superhero characters, explaining that finding the balance between moving the story forward and honoring those already-beloved characters can be “very difficult.” “It’s a…
body: Russo also said that he and his brother and co-director Joe have “a lot of respect for the storytelling journey that these characters have had up to this point.” “That’s part of their magic, a big part of their magic. But at the same time, we need to surprise ourselves in terms of who those characters are, where they can go, what they can do, what can happen, and in doing that, we hopefully surprise audiences as well.”

The director’s comments come nearly a year after an “Avengers: Doomsday” trailer spotlighted a much more serious Thor ( Chris Hemsworth ) than Marvel fans had seen in 2022’s “ Thor: Love and Thunder.” The Taika Waititi-directed film performed well at the box office upon its release, but it divided fans who felt the character had become, in Hemsworth’s own words, “too silly.”

articles.title: Neil Patrick Harris to Star in ‘Damn Yankees’ Broadway Revival
articles.summary: A revival of “Damn Yankees,” starring Neil Patrick Harris and Julianne Hough, will open next spring on Broadway. It’s the first Broadway revival of “Damn Yankees” in more than 30 years.
body: “Damn Yankees,” which revolves around a middle-aged man who makes a Faustian bargain for his losing baseball team to somehow beat the unstoppable New York Yankees, debuted on Broadway in 1955 with Robert Shafer, Gwen Verdon, Ray Walston and Stephen Douglass. It won seven Tony Awards, including best musical. Richard Adler and Jerry Ross wrote the music and lyrics, with a book by George Abbott and Douglass Wallop. The show was last revived on Broadway in 1993 with Jarrod Emick, Bebe Neuwirth and Victor Garber.
Harris will play the devil in disguise known as Applegate, Hough is making her Broadway debut as Joe’s wife Lola and Austin Scott is playing Young Joe. The rest of the cast has yet to be announced.

Harris won a Tony for the 2014 revival of “Hedwig and the Angry Inch” and has hosted the Tony Awards several times. He was recently on Broadway in “Art,” a play revival in which he starred alongside James Corden and Bobby Cannavale.

articles.title: Angelina Jolie's Underrated Action Thriller Got A Well-Deserved Perfect Review From Roger Ebert
articles.summary: Roger Ebert was a big supporter of this Angelina Jolie action thriller, which was something of a hit despite its relative obscurity nowadays.
body: "Salt" was written by Kurt Wimmer, a hardworking Hollywood veteran who made a proper name for himself when he penned and directed the somewhat overlooked 2002 dystopian sci-fi action flick "Equilibrium" starring Christian Bale. Wimmer has since written not-very-good remakes like "Total Recall," "Point Break," and "Children of the Corn," but with "Salt," he was firing on all cylinders. It's a spy thriller par excellence. Which is to say that, yes, it's a little absurd, but the stakes are high, the main character is great, and the stunts are spectacular. This film is the kind of entertainment that should be every blockbuster's birthright yet is rarely actually made.

But don't take my word for it. Ebert gave "Salt" four out of four stars, even titling his review, "Now HERE's what I mean by an action movie." As he put it, "['Salt'] does all the things I can't stand in bad movies, and does them in a good one. It's like a rebuke to all the lousy action movie directors who've been banging pots and pans together in our skulls." High praise indeed.

articles.title: ‘A joyful place’: a new museum coaxes Austrians to embrace The Sound of Music
articles.summary: Sixty years after the film’s release, Salzburg is embracing a Hollywood classic it once kept at arm’s length. Let’s start at the very beginning – famously, a very good place to start.
body: Just two decades after the second world war, a Hollywood crew descended on Salzburg with stars, show tunes and a compelling, essentially true story of love and opposition to Adolf Hitler: The Sound of Music.
The Austrian city, still economically and morally devastated from the Nazi period, wasn’t quite ready to receive them.

Although director Robert Wise was free to make use of the glorious Alpine settings and the old town’s historical facades, scenes such as soldiers marching across the central Residenzplatz under swastika flags made municipal authorities deeply uneasy.
When the film premiered in 1965, it ran for a couple of weeks, closed for lack of ticket sales and largely disappeared from local memory. That is until the tour buses started coming.

articles.title: Roger Ebert Gave A Perfect Score To This Woody Harrelson Crime Thriller No One Talks About
articles.summary: The great Roger Ebert once gave a perfect rating to a 2012 crime thriller starring Woody Harrelson that no one really talks about these days.
body: In 2012, Woody Harrelson starred in "Rampart," a crime drama that, though well-reviewed, was a box office bomb. Still, a perfect review from Roger Ebert surely helped partially make up for the film's commercial performance, with the esteemed critic heaping praise on this gritty tale of a corrupt LAPD veteran who's forced to reckon with his shady legacy.

One man who certainly wouldn't have forgotten the movie, however, is Ebert. The critic, who passed away at the age of 70 in 2013, gave "Rampart" a full four stars, praising Harrelson for his performance as a morally bankrupt crooked cop backed into a corner. While not everybody found it to be one of the greatest thrillers of the 21st century, it should at least be remembered more widely than it is, and, according to Ebert, might even deserve a spot on that list.

articles.title: Before Supernatural, Jeffrey Dean Morgan Appeared In This Short-Lived '90s Sci-Fi Series
articles.summary: Before his recurring role on Supernatural, Jeffrey Dean Morgan had a part in this '90s sci-fi series that was quickly canceled.
body: Jeffrey Dean Morgan is one of those actors who was kind of a late bloomer, but made the most of it when his career finally started to catch on. He had a very memorable role on "Supernatural," which ended after a record-setting 15 seasons on The CW. He's also known for his work in movies like "Rampage" and "Fall," among many others. But long before any of that, he starred in a very short-lived '90s sci-fi series.

"The Burning Zone" aired for just a single season on UPN between 1996 and 1997 and was swiftly canceled thereafter. The series centers on Dr. Daniel Cassian (Michael Harris) who is appointed by White House to lead a small top secret federal biological task force of leading scientists to investigate biochemical threats and emergencies. Morgan played a member of the team, Dr. Edward Marcase.

This came at a time when "The X-Files," one of the best sci-fi TV shows of all time, was at the height of its powers. Naturally, other networks tried to copy that success. "The Burning Zone," created by Coleman Luck, was very much attempting to capture a similar vibe, except with chemical and biological threats, as opposed to aliens and the supernatural. The problem? It wasn't very good.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Says It Would Be “Tough” for His Batman to Interact With Other Characters in James Gunn’s DCU
articles.summary: The actor plays Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves’ 'The Batman' and the upcoming sequel.
body: Robert Pattinson doesn’t see his version of Batman interacting with other DC superheroes within James Gunn ‘s cinematic universe.

While Batman and Superman have one of the most famous friendships in DC Comics, the Primetime star recently explained to LADbible why it would be “tough” for director Matt Reeves ’ version of Bruce Wayne to exist in Gunn’s DCU, such as with David Corenswet’s Superman.

“I think it would be kind of tough to have this version of Bruce outside of that world. It’s one of the only characters, I guess because of the length of the shoots but also it’s such a specific kind of [style], the tone of it gets inside you,” Pattinson said. “I remember that happened to me the last time I did it, it took a while. You’re just in the dark, the whole time. Both mood-wise and light-wise, I can’t see anything for like months. It does affect you; like you feel strange afterwards.” Related Stories.
